report.summary: The level 2 mine upgrade is queued and currently active, due in about 11 game minutes. It has not finished yet.
report.whatChanged: The build command was committed. The receipt confirms that 30,000 marked iron and 15,000 marked silver were charged. The builder in slot 1 is working on the mine; slot 2 is free. The mine itself is still shown at level 1, so completion is not confirmed. No trade or contact was proposed or signed, and there are no active supply contracts. Nothing was rejected.
report.nextDecision: Wait for the mine upgrade to finish, then review the updated state before choosing another build or considering trade.
report.reasonToReturn: Return when the mine upgrade is finished so you can choose the next growth move with current resource and building information.
report.confusion: The plan said the upgrade was affordable using its listed cost of 50 iron and 25 silver, while the receipt reports charges of 30,000 marked iron and 15,000 marked silver. The record shows the command committed, but does not explain that unit difference.

report.whatChanged: The queue command was committed, and 24,000 marked iron plus 12,000 marked silver were charged. The farm is still level 1 while it is being built; builder slot 1 is active, with about 11 game minutes remaining. The upgrade is therefore queued and active as construction, but not finished. No contact or supply contract was created. Nothing was rejected, proposed, or signed in the receipts or current state.
report.nextDecision: Wait for the farm upgrade to finish, then check its level and updated production before choosing another move.
report.reasonToReturn: Return when construction is due so you can confirm the farm reached level 2 and decide what to build or pursue diplomatically next.
report.confusion: The plan called the upgrade affordable at 24,000 iron and 12,000 silver, but the after-state lists level 2 costs of only 40 iron and 20 silver in whole units. The receipt confirms what was charged, but the supplied facts do not explain that discrepancy.

report.summary: The Farm upgrade to level 2 was accepted and is now active as construction, due in about 11 game minutes. It has not finished yet.
report.whatChanged: The receipt says COMMITTED and records 24,000 marked Iron and 12,000 marked Silver charged. The after-state confirms a level-2 Farm build instruction in builder slot 1. The Farm itself is still listed at level 1 until construction completes. No trade or contact was proposed, signed, or made active. Nothing was rejected or merely queued without acceptance: the command committed, and the build is underway.
report.nextDecision: Wait for the Farm construction to finish, then check its level and the resulting production before choosing another move.

Also, the receipt has no committed event IDs, but the active builder and consequence records confirm the construction instruction is running.

The updated state shows builder slot 1 working on the Mine with about 11 game minutes remaining; the Mine itself is still level 1 until construction finishes. report.confusion: The receipt says COMMITTED, while the state calls the build active. These fit together: the command was accepted and construction is underway, but the upgrade is not finished. The charged figures are marked units, while the resource display also reports whole units and founding allowances, so the separate numbers can be hard to compare.

report.summary: Both upgrade commands were accepted and are now underway: the farm and mine are each upgrading to level 2, with about 11 game minutes remaining. Neither upgrade is finished yet.
report.whatChanged: The server committed both queues and charged 24,000 iron plus 12,000 silver for the farm, and 30,000 iron plus 15,000 silver for the mine. Both builders are active. The buildings still show level 1 because construction has not settled. There are no contacts, proposals, or supply contracts in the supplied state.
report.nextDecision: Wait for construction to finish, then check the receipts and builder availability before choosing another upgrade. Grain is low in ordinary stock but nets 22 per hour; iron nets 20 and silver 10 per hour. Construction spent from founding allowance first, which cannot be used for cold contacts or trade.
report.reasonToReturn: Return after roughly 11 game minutes to see whether both upgrades finished and review the new production rates.
report.confusion: The plan described upgrades costing 40 iron and 20 silver for the farm, and 50 iron and 25 silver for the mine, but receipts report much larger charged amounts. The supplied facts do not explain that difference. The receipts confirm the charges and committed queues, while the active builder records show the work is still in progress.

report.summary: The mine upgrade finished. No actions were submitted, so nothing was queued, proposed, signed, or newly made active.
report.whatChanged: The mine is now level 2. Both builders are free, and a farm upgrade to level 2 is affordable at 40 iron and 20 silver. Current net grain production is 22 per hour. There are no contacts, requests, offers, or supply contracts.

report.confusion: The plan says to wait because it lacks a farm action example and construction is not allowed, but the current mandate explicitly allows building queues. The receipts are empty, so no action was submitted; affordability alone does not show that a queue was attempted or accepted.

The receipt confirms the request committed, but does not say it was accepted. No request was rejected, queued, finished, proposed, signed, or made active as a trade.
